content:
More than 36,500 ballots have been cast in Webb County through the first 10 days of early voting, according to the Laredo Morning Times. The exact total reported was 36,573 ballots, comprising 35,793 in-person votes and 780 mail-in ballots.

On day 10 itself, Wednesday, 3,418 ballots were cast — 3,364 in person and 54 by mail, according to election officials. The busiest day so far was Monday, October 19, with 5,343 ballots, while the lowest day was Sunday, with 1,913. The busiest location overall was the Laredo Fire Department Administrative Center, with 11,300 votes; it also led on Wednesday with 857 votes.

The day-10 figure continues a steady climb: the county elections office had reported more than 33,000 early voters as of October 28, as reported by KGNS, meaning the count kept rising into the final stretch of early voting.

Early voting ends Friday, October 30, at 8 p.m. — the last early chance to vote before Election Day on Tuesday, November 3. During early voting, registered voters may cast a ballot at any early-voting location in the county; Election Day locations and hours can differ, so voters should confirm their site before heading out.

The November 3 ballot includes the Laredo mayor's race, City Council seats in Districts 1, 2, 3 and 6, and Municipal Court Judge Place 1, along with county, state and federal contests. If no candidate in a race wins more than 50 percent, the top two advance to a December runoff. Polls on Election Day are open 7 a.m. to 7 p.m.

Sources:

  • Laredo Morning Times, "First 10 days of early voting bring more than 36,500 ballots in Webb County," October 29, 2026
  • KGNS, "Webb County elections office reports more than 33,000 early voters so far," October 28, 2026

title: Webb County early voting tops 36,500 ballots through day 10
